SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: CAN - NRCan MRDEM 30m DTM - single national COG
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Medium Resolution DEM, the national 30m terrain model (CDEM successor) as one 84 GB COG on NRCan's CanElevation bucket - CORS *, range requests, LZW, 10 overviews. EPSG:3979 (Canada Atlas Lambert), so pinned to titiler. Nodata -32767. Open Government Licence - Canada.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: CHE - swisstopo swissALTIRegio 10m - single national COG
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: The whole of Switzerland in one 10 GB COG - 55000x43000, six overview levels, 256px tiles, CORS open, range requests supported. A rare case of a national DEM published as a single fetchable file rather than tens of thousands of tiles. EPSG:2056, so it is pinned to titiler (cogViaTitiler) - the in-browser COG reader assumes 3857 and would misplace it. No-data is +3.4e38, a POSITIVE Float32 max. Note swisstopo also publishes swissALTI3D at 0.5m and swissSURFACE3D at 0.5m, but only as per-tile COGs indexed by STAC - and Mapterhorn already ingests the 0.5m, so this 10m single file is for convenience, not resolution. swisstopo open data, attribution required.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: CHE - swisstopo Terrain 3D (quantized mesh, keyless)
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: swisstopo's own Cesium terrain, and the one open quantized-mesh service worth having: no token, CORS open, and measured down to level 18 over the Matterhorn where Cesium World Terrain runs out around 13-14. Built from swissALTI3D, so it is the same lineage as the swissALTI Regio COG in this library but as a TIN. The mesh is rasterised per tile in the browser (see /dev/quantized-mesh-protocol). Heights are ELLIPSOIDAL, as the quantized-mesh format requires - roughly +38 m against an orthometric reference on a coarse check, consistent with the ~49 m Swiss geoid separation - so absolute values read high while shape and shading are right. MapLibre's own 3D-terrain example uses this same endpoint.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: CZE - CUZK DMP 0.5m (surface) - ImageServer raw Float32

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: CZE - CUZK DMR 5G 2m - ImageServer raw Float32
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Nationwide 2m lidar terrain model (DMR 5G), native EPSG:3857. Verified Snezka 1603.4 m against a true 1603.3 m and Prague 188.8-303.4 m. SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: FIN - NLS/Paituli DEM 10m - WCS raw Float32

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: FRA - Ground change: IGN Lidar HD DTM (2021+) - RGE ALTI DTM (2009-2020) - derived

Use the hypsometric ramp's Symmetric Range so gain and loss read as opposite colours, and expect a few metres of noise where RGE ALTI is the coarse 5 m photogrammetric grid rather than lidar - the auto-offset button on this row re-centres the difference on zero for the area on screen. Both operands are added with it; each is a raw Float32 WMS.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Building and canopy height over the Msimbazi floodplain: the drone surface minus the LiDAR ground. Two different sensors and campaigns, so use the auto-offset in the hypsometric section to re-centre bare ground on zero first.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - JAXA ALOS World 3D 30m (AW3D30) - VRT
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: JAXA's global 30 m DSM, mirrored by OpenTopography as a single global VRT over per-degree COGs (10 MB index, CORS-open, verified). A genuinely INDEPENDENT global surface model from Copernicus GLO-30 and SRTM - different sensor (ALOS PRISM optical stereo), different epoch (2006-2011) - which is what makes it useful here: difference it against Mapterhorn or GLO-30 and the disagreement between two global DSMs is the signal. Readable either through titiler or in-browser (vrt:// parses the 10 MB index once, then Range-reads the per-degree COGs; usable z8-12). Free with attribution to JAXA.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - Google GEM-15 DTM 15m bare earth (2022-2024 stereo satellite) - COG cells
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Google Research's GEM-15 (experimental, under review, CC BY 4.0, released October 2026): a near-global DSM and DTM at 15 m from sub-metre optical stereo satellite imagery acquired through 2024, mostly 30 cm Pleiades Neo of 2022-2024. This is the DTM: bare earth predicted at 1 m by a deep-learning model under the canopy and the buildings, then aggregated to 15 m. Orthometric heights on EGM96. 60S to 84N, without Russia, China, Mongolia, Greenland and Antarctica; India is offset for regulatory reasons; water, snow and ice are masked. One COG per 1x1 degree cell in its own UTM zone, about 13 500 cells: the reader lists the cells a tile touches, reads them through the Cloud Storage JSON API media endpoint (the plain bucket URL has no CORS) and composites them, so expect a second or two per tile the first time and holes where a cell does not exist. Dense forest lowers the DTM's accuracy, and regional vertical offsets of several metres against lidar have been reported. Usable z7-13.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - Google GEM-15 DSM 15m surface (2022-2024 stereo satellite) - COG cells
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Google Research's GEM-15 surface model: the mean elevation of the native 0.5 m stereo surface within each 15 m cell, canopy and roofs included (the file's other bands, the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles and the standard deviation, are not read). Same coverage, datum and cell layout as the GEM-15 DTM, but the file holds five bands pixel-interleaved, so a browser read of band 1 decodes all five: about 3 s a window against 1 s for the DTM, and a cold viewport can take a minute. Read in the browser by default; switch this source (or the global COG protocol setting) to titiler and each cell is served by titiler instead, about 1 s a tile. Difference the two for a canopy and building height surface. Usable z7-13.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - Google GEM-15 nDSM 15m: DSM minus DTM (canopy and building height) - derived
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: GEM-15's surface minus its own bare-earth model: a near-global 15 m height-above-ground surface, trees and buildings as positive values, open ground near zero. Both sides come from the same stereo imagery and the same datum, so leave the offset at 0. Usable z7-13.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - Copernicus GLO-30 DSM 30m (COP30) - VRT
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: ESA's Copernicus DEM GLO-30: the TanDEM-X radar surface model of 2011-2015 edited and infilled to one global 30 m DSM, the model Mapterhorn serves wherever a country has nothing finer. OpenTopography mirrors it as one global VRT over per-degree COGs (11.7 MB index, Float32, CORS-open, same host and reader as AW3D30). Having it as its own source lets you difference it against the national models, against AW3D30 (optical stereo of 2006-2011 against radar of 2011-2015) and against GEM-15. Free, attribution to ESA and Copernicus. Usable z8-12.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - NASADEM 30m (SRTM reprocessed, 60S-61N) - VRT
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: NASA's 2020 reprocessing of the February 2000 SRTM radar mission with improved phase unwrapping, ICESat control and void filling from ASTER and AW3D30: the cleanest SRTM there is, 1 arc-second, 60S to 61N. Int16 metres, nodata -32768. OpenTopography VRT over per-degree COGs (6.5 MB index, CORS-open). An independent third global model next to GLO-30 and AW3D30, and the one to difference for 2000-era surfaces. Usable z8-12.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - SRTM GL1 30m (2000 radar, 60S-60N) - VRT
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: The original SRTM 1 arc-second global release (void-filled, 2014) of the February 2000 Shuttle Radar Topography Mission, 60S to 60N, Int16 metres, nodata -32768. The surface of the year 2000 as it was measured: difference it against GLO-30 or GEM-15 for two decades of change at 30 m, keeping in mind the radar penetrates canopy only partly. OpenTopography VRT over per-degree COGs (6.2 MB index, CORS-open). Usable z8-12.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Europe - EU DTM 30m (OpenGeoHub ensemble, bare earth) - VRT
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: OpenGeoHub's continental DTM of 2022: an ensemble machine-learning bare-earth model trained on ICESat-2 and GEDI ground returns over the Copernicus DEM and other covariates, 30 m, ETRS89 LAEA (EPSG:3035), the whole continent from the Atlantic to the Urals. OpenTopography VRT (one source, CORS-open; the reader reprojects LAEA in the browser). The continental counterpart of GEDTM30, and a DTM to difference against the GLO-30 surface for canopy and buildings. Usable z8-12.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - GEDTM30 bare earth 30m (OpenGeoHub) - VRT, in-browser
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: The same GEDTM30 as the titiler-pinned COG entry (OpenGeoHub's 2025 global ensemble DTM at 30 m, EPSG:4326, nodata 3.4e38), read in the browser through OpenTopography's mirror: a one-source VRT over the mirrored COG on a CORS-open host, so every client-side mode and the export work without titiler. Usable z8-12.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - SRTM15+ V2.6 topography and bathymetry 15 arc-sec (~450 m) - VRT
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Scripps's SRTM15+ (Tozer et al.), land topography from SRTM and ASTER and seafloor bathymetry from ship soundings and satellite altimetry gravity, one grid pole to pole at 15 arc-seconds (about 450 m at the equator). The only entry here with the ocean floor below sea level: trenches, ridges and shelves in hillshade and hypsometry. Float32, nodata NaN. OpenTopography VRT (41 KB index, CORS-open). Usable z4-8.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - Difference: AW3D30 - Mapterhorn - derived
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Two independent global elevation models subtracted: JAXA's ALOS World 3D against whatever Mapterhorn serves here (a national dataset where it has one, Copernicus GLO-30 where it does not). Over GLO-30 areas this is optical-stereo minus radar and mostly shows canopy and sensor disagreement; over a national LiDAR area it shows how far a 30 m global model is from surveyed ground. Use Symmetric Range, and the difference offset to remove the datum constant first.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: USA - New York statewide LiDAR DEM 1m - ImageServer raw Float32
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: New York State's 1 m LiDAR mosaic (newest survey on top), dynamic exportImage as Float32. SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Lithuania's national LiDAR terrain model at a 1 m grid, from the National Land Service data, published by HNIT-Baltic as a public ArcGIS Online item. SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: IDN - BIG DEMNAS ~8m - ImageServer raw Float32

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: ITA - INGV TINITALY 10m - WCS 2.0 raw Float32
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: TINITALY 1.1, the de-facto national DEM of Italy (INGV; IGM publishes no open raw service). CC BY 4.0. WCS 2.0.1 rejects BBOX with HTTP 504, so the __wcs2subset marker rewrites it to subset=X()/Y() plus scaleSize - see WCS2SUBSET_RE in lib/float32dem-protocol.ts. Sentinel -9999. Regione Sardegna also serves a 1m WCS (webgis2.regione.sardegna.it/geoserverraster/ows, coverage raster:DTM_1M_MOSAICO_ALTIMETRIA) but it covers only about half the island in patchy blocks, so it is not shipped. Requests between z6 and z9 return 504 after ~60s; z10 works (~4s), hence minzoom 10.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: JPN - GSI/GSJ seamless elevation tiles 5-10m - Terrain-RGB
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: The Geological Survey of Japan (AIST) re-serves GSI's national elevation tiles as standard Mapbox Terrain-RGB: DEM5A/B/C (5m) where available, DEM10B (10m) elsewhere, Hyogo LiDAR at z16-17, with ASTER GDEM and GEBCO bathymetry outside Japan at low zoom. Note the {z}/{y}/{x} order in the path. GSI's own tiles use a signed 24-bit x0.01 packing no raster-dem encoding can express - this conversion is what makes Japan loadable here. z16+ returns HTTP 400 outside Hyogo, hence maxzoom 15. Verified: Mt Fuji 3773.8 m (true 3776). CORS *. GSI content usage terms (attribution GSI / GSJ-AIST); GSJ marks the service experimental.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: MEX - INEGI CEM 3.0 - TMS custom RGB encoding
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Continuo de Elevaciones Mexicano, nationwide ~15m. SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: NZL - LINZ national 1m LiDAR DEM - Terrain-RGB
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: LINZ Basemaps: national 8m DEM with regional 1m LiDAR mosaicked in. The only true Terrain-RGB service published by any national mapping agency. CC BY 4.0 LINZ, attribution required. Two non-obvious requirements: pipeline=terrain-rgb (without it the endpoint 404s) and an api= key. The key is NOT issued by a server - LINZ Basemaps mints it client-side as "c" + a lowercase ULID and caches it in localStorage, so there is no registration, login or email. The one shipped here was minted the same way and can be replaced with your own at basemaps.linz.govt.nz if it ever gets rate-limited.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Uruguay's national 30m terrain model from IDEuy (AGESIC). WCS 2.0.1 on GeoServer, rewritten by the __wcs2subset marker with the OGC i/j scaleSize URIs. Slow - 7-11 s per window - but genuine Float32. Untagged nodata -32767 (sea), caught by the floor. Requests entirely outside the extent return an OWS exception, which simply leaves those tiles empty. Verified: Mt Whitney 4417.6 m (true 4421), Death Valley -85.1 m (true -86). Public domain. NOTE: cold requests can take ~16s or return 502/504; repeats are cached and return in ~0.2s.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: USA - USGS 3DEP - WMS raw Float32
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: The same 3DEP seamless mosaic as the ImageServer entry, through the ArcGIS WMS front end of that image service: GetMap with FORMAT=image/tiff returns a single-band Float32 GeoTIFF (verified 2458 m over the Sierra), so it decodes exactly like the exportImage route. Kept as an alternative when the REST endpoint misbehaves. Public domain.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - Esri World Elevation 3D (land only, ocean at 0 m) - LERC
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: The land-only variant of the Esri blend that ships as the built-in "Esri World Elevation" source: identical on land, but the ocean reads a flat 0 m instead of the seafloor. Worth choosing when a coastline should be a hard edge - a hypsometric ramp keyed to land relief is wrecked by a -7000 m trench sharing its range. Verified ORTHOMETRIC, not ellipsoidal: six points across an Innsbruck tile average -0.6 m against a reference DEM (spread 18 m, which is terrain sampling noise between two models in steep ground), so unlike ArcticDEM/REMA it needs no geoid correction. Ocean reads a flat 0 m; use the TopoBathy entry for real bathymetry. Real data to z16-17 worldwide (the service declares LOD 16); beyond that every pixel comes back masked, which lerc:// writes as flat 0 m with alpha 254 rather than a pit. NOTE the service's exportImage endpoint is useless anonymously - it only ever answers from a ~2.5 km overview (WorldDTM_OV256), rendering an alpine valley as a smooth ramp even with an explicit fine pixelSize. The /tile pyramid is the only anonymous route to real resolution. LICENCE: this is an Esri ArcGIS service. It answers without a token and with CORS open, but Esri's Terms of Use contemplate use with ArcGIS products; consuming it from a non-Esri client is not clearly granted. Check before relying on it in anything published.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - ANADEM AI bare-earth DTM from the GLO-30 DSM, South America 30m - single COG
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: All of South America in one COG - 187853x262864 with 10 overview levels, CORS open, range requests supported. AI terrain model: the same 30m grid as Copernicus GLO-30, which is a SURFACE model, machine-learning corrected to BARE EARTH. Under Amazon canopy GLO-30 measures the treetops and can sit tens of metres high; Mapterhorn only carries that surface over South America, so this is the better ground model there - same resolution, but terrain rather than canopy. maxzoom 15 (30m is z12.4): tiles up to z15 are upsampled by titiler with bilinear resampling, which reads as a smooth surface; with maxzoom 13 MapLibre overzoomed the last DEM tile itself and the hillshade showed every 30m cell as a flat block. EPSG:4674, so it is pinned to titiler (cogViaTitiler): the in-browser COG reader assumes 3857, misplaces it, and reads its degree-sized pixels as metres - which is what made the camera lock at z19. Nodata -9999. See https://opentopography.org/news/new-machine-learning-derived-digital-terrain-models

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - Digital Earth Africa GLO-30 (Africa + Arabia) 30m - WCS 2.1 raw Float32
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Continent-wide coverage of Africa and Arabia from one endpoint - the only keyless live raw-elevation service found for any African country. Copernicus GLO-30 (~30m) re-served by Digital Earth Africa; a continental programme re-publishing a global DEM, not a sovereign national product. CC-BY 4.0 (DE Africa) / Copernicus free-use. WCS 2.1 needs the __wcs2subset rewrite, with scaleSize in plain axis labels - this server returns HTTP 500 for the OGC i/j URIs that TINITALY requires. Verified: Addis Ababa 2206-2793 m, Kilimanjaro tile peaks near 5895 m.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - EMODnet Bathymetry (European seas) ~115m - WCS raw Float32
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: European Marine Observation and Data Network digital bathymetry 2024, 1/16 arc-minute (~115 m) mean depth of all European seas, negative below sea level; land is NaN and fills to 0. WCS 1.0 with a WMS-shaped BBOX so it needs no rewrite. Older releases are coverage=emodnet:mean_2016/2018/2020/2022. Verified central North Sea -32.5 m. CC BY 4.0, attribution EMODnet Bathymetry Consortium.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - GEDTM30 AI bare-earth DTM from the GLO-30 DSM, worldwide 30m - single COG
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: OpenLandMap / OpenGeoHub's global 30m terrain model, one 432 GB COG (1.3 million x 540 thousand pixels, 11 overviews) with CORS * and range requests. Like ANADEM it is an AI terrain model: Copernicus GLO-30 is a SURFACE model (it measures canopy and roofs), and this is machine-learning corrected towards bare earth using ALOS and GEDI spaceborne LiDAR. Mapterhorn only carries the GLO-30 surface where it has no national data, so anywhere outside its 32 countries this is the better ground model - same grid, but the terrain rather than the treetops. EPSG:4326, pinned to titiler; titiler.xyz answers HTTP 500 for z4-z5 windows of this file, hence minzoom 6. Nodata +3.4e38, and it MUST be passed to titiler (titilerNodata): with the default nodata=0 override the sentinel reaches the terrainrgb encoder on every tile that touches the sea and titiler answers 500 (larger than 256 ** 3), so the whole coastline was missing. Verified: Mont Blanc 4805.6 m, Everest 8742 m (3x3 max). CC BY 4.0, Zenodo 15689805.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - EGM96 geoid undulation 15' (ellipsoid - geoid separation)
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Not terrain: the SEPARATION between the WGS84 ellipsoid and the EGM96 geoid, in metres, -107 m at the Indian Ocean low to +85 m near Papua New Guinea. This is the number that makes an ellipsoidal source (Cesium World Terrain, ArcticDEM, REMA, swisstopo quantized mesh) read high against an orthometric one (Mapterhorn, AWS, Esri, most national DEMs). Best viewed with the hypsometric ramp's Symmetric Range so zero sits at the neutral colour. NGA's own grid, redistributed by the PROJ CDN (public domain), EPSG:4979 so it is routed through titiler. 15 arc-minutes is coarse by design - the geoid is a long-wavelength field.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - EGM2008 geoid undulation 2.5' (ellipsoid - geoid separation)
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: The same quantity as the EGM96 entry at six times the resolution (2.5 arc-minutes), from the newer EGM2008 model - use this one to check an ellipsoidal source's offset somewhere specific, and the 15' one for a world view. PROJ CDN, public domain, EPSG:4979 via titiler.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - Smart Maps GEL NASADEM 30m Terrain-RGB z2-12 (CC0) - PMTiles
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: UN Smart Maps Group's Global Elevation Tiles: NASADEM (SRTM completed with ASTER GDEM and ALOS, 30 m, 60N-56S) at z6-12 and ISCGM Global Map at z2-5, as Mapbox Terrain-RGB WebP tiles in one 182 GB PMTiles archive on source.coop. Read through the app's pmtiles:// protocol (range requests into the archive, no tile server). CC0, which is its reason to exist: a worldwide DEM with no attribution or licence constraints, for redistribution and derived products. Coarser and older than Mapterhorn; useful when the licence matters.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: ART - Impasto: Harm Belt's Almond Blossom, height scan (0.25 um units, fake-geo) - PMTiles
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: A painting as terrain: the 24 cm Almond Blossom (Harm Belt, after Van Gogh) scanned by a Keyence condition-assessment scanner at 3072 px per 24 mm, 32768 x 32768 px, stretched over the whole Web Mercator world the way the non-geo relief recipe does. One PMTiles archive of 1024 px PNG tiles, z0-5, MapLibre custom encoding value = R*65536 + G*256 + B, integers of 0.25 micrometres (range about 9000-45000, 2 to 11 mm of impasto), read as raw units here, as on impasto.dev, so slopes and relief are relative: use exaggeration (their viewer uses 12) and the hypsometric Set from viewport. The host only allows impasto.dev to read the archive: a browser needs a CORS-allowing extension or a proxy. Format notes on the PMTiles page of the dev docs.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - Open Waters Seascape Bathymetry - Terrarium
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Open Waters Seascape: the seafloor only, a mosaic of 34 open bathymetry sources (GEBCO 2026, EMODnet 2024, NOAA, AusBathyTopo and regional surveys). Global at about 450 m (zoom 8), regional detail down to about 8 m (zoom 14) where a survey exists. Depths are negative metres; land is not elevation but a flat code (0 water of unknown depth, 1 drying foreshore, 2 land), so pair it with a land source in a split view. The datum varies by source (chart datum or about mean sea level). Terrarium WebP, 512 px tiles, keyless, CORS-open. Not for navigation. Each source keeps its own licence (mostly CC BY 4.0, CC0 or public domain); credit Open Waters.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - PGC ArcticDEM 2m (Arctic, ellipsoidal) - ImageServer raw Float32
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Polar Geospatial Center's ArcticDEM mosaic, 2m stereo-photogrammetric surface model of all land north of 60 N (Greenland, Svalbard, Iceland, northern Scandinavia, Siberia, Alaska, Canadian Arctic). SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global South - Google Open Buildings 2.5D height 0.5m, 2016 - COG tiles
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Google Open Buildings 2.5D Temporal, the only PERIODIC open building-height product: one raster per year from 2016 to 2023 at 0.5 m, inferred from Sentinel-2 and Landsat over Africa, South and Southeast Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean (nothing north of 38N). Band 2 of three is building_height, nodata -99: a building-height surface above bare ground, not terrain, 0 over open country. Google ships each year as 1 173 Earth Engine image manifests (one per S2 cell and UTM zone); the reader picks the one or two manifests a tile touches from a committed 80 KB index, fetches each (950 KB, kept for the session) through the Cloud Storage JSON API media endpoint and reads its 25 000 px COG tiles in the browser, see the Cell-routed sources dev page. Rio, Lagos, Jakarta, Mumbai, Mexico City are good places to look. Usable z11-18. 2016 edition, the first year of the series: difference it against 2023 to read seven years of building growth.

SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global South - Difference: Open Buildings 2.5D 2023 - 2016 (building growth) - derived
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: Seven years of building growth as elevation change: the 2023 Open Buildings 2.5D height raster minus the 2016 one, anywhere the product covers. SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.name: Global - Meta / WRI Canopy Height 1m (CHM v2, tree height above ground) - COG cells via titiler
SAMPLE_TERRAIN_SOURCES.description: High Resolution Canopy Height Maps by Meta and the World Resources Institute, version 2 (2026, DINOv3 model on sub-metre Maxar imagery, most of it from 2017 to 2020): the height of the tree canopy above the ground in whole metres, 0 over open land and water. A height-above-ground surface, not terrain: use it like an nDSM (colour relief, contours, 3D with exaggeration). One COG per Web Mercator quadkey cell on Meta's public S3 bucket, 213 109 cells of zoom 10 at 1.19 m and a 10 m mean derivative in 4 376 cells of zoom 7. The bucket answers Range requests but sends no CORS header, so the browser cannot read the files itself: every tile is asked from titiler (the endpoint in Settings), the 10 m cells to zoom 14 and the 1 m cells from zoom 15, about a second a tile the first time. A committed 133 KB index says which cells exist. Known limits: a false signal of about 10 m over polar ice and snow north of 70N, image-date seams, and heights that saturate in the tallest forests. Usable z6-17. CC BY 4.0, Meta and WRI, imagery (c) Maxar.

A 107k x 33k mosaic without overviews: titiler serves it from zoom 13 (a second or two a tile); further out the read fails, so the view lands at zoom 13.
